posts.heading: September 29, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 21 species and 318 feeder visits, marking a slight dip in volume from the seven-day average of 326.9 visits while maintaining a similar diversity count compared to the previous week. The regulars remained consistent, with Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees, and House Finches dominating the feeder activity as seen across all seven days of observation. Activity levels were comparable to the recent days, with the visitation count falling between the quiet weekend and the busier early week.

Audio detections totaled 281, which is lower than the weekly average of 314.6. American Goldfinches and Brown Thrasher returned to the list after absences of nine and eleven days, respectively, joining the steady chorus of Eastern Towhnees and Carolina Chickadees. No new species were first heard at the station.

Visually, the day concluded with a Northern Cardinal spotted just two minutes after sunset, while the first confident visual record occurred 17 minutes before sunrise. Gray Catbird and Mourning Dove appeared in the visual data, with the latter seen on six of the last seven days.

posts.heading: September 28, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 389 feeder visits and 21 species, a busy day that exceeded the previous week's average of 289 visits and 18.6 species. Regulars like the Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal held steady, with Tufted Titmouse accounting for 152 confident visual visits. A Tufted Titmouse was observed on a tube feeder, and a solitary White-breasted Nuthatch was seen feeding in the wooded backyard.

Ruby-throated Hummingbirds, recorded on each of the last seven days, were absent today, as were Red-bellied Woodpeckers and Pileated Woodpeckers. No new species were heard or seen for the first time at this station, and no new audio source changes affected the detections.
